title: Count threshold gates are linear thresholds
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $k$ be a natural number. On the sign cube, the function that outputs $1$ when at least $k$ coordinates indexed by $S$ are positive and outputs $-1$ otherwise is a linear threshold function: there are real coefficients and a real bias whose threshold sign gives this function at every input.
hypotheses_covered: A finite set $S$ of coordinates among $0,\ldots,n-1$
